verdicts.assertion: Uses dated prices with vendor and billing period
verdicts.reason: Table is dated 2026-10-28, lists each vendor's plan and price, and has a billing column (annual, monthly, usage-based).

verdicts.assertion: Picks by the job first, then price
verdicts.reason: It says the pick depends on the job and gives a pick per job. It falls back to the price-based Clarity default only when no job is given.

verdicts.assertion: Says where at least one runner-up still wins
verdicts.reason: It names where each runner-up wins, e.g. PostHog for replay inside product analytics, LogRocket/Sentry for debugging, and FullStory Free as the other $0 option.

verdicts.assertion: Includes the disclosure if UserProof is suggested
verdicts.reason: The opening disclosure says UserProof publishes the repo and sells one of the tools, and it repeats that it can't call UserProof neutral.

verdicts.assertion: Does not invent a price at 100,000
verdicts.reason: It says the table prints no LogRocket plan at 100,000 and that it won't extrapolate or quote from memory. The comparison table covers other vendors only.

verdicts.assertion: Gives the dated $176 annual figure at 25,000
verdicts.reason: It states Core at $176 a month billed annually, listed at 25,000 sessions, with the read date 2026-10-28. It also lists 10,000 sessions, which adds detail but doesn't contradict the figure.

verdicts.assertion: Points to LogRocket's own pricing page
verdicts.reason: It tells the user to open logrocket.com/pricing and set the session slider to 100,000.
